explanation:
[EFFECT] The hour of the day has a strongly non-monotonic, double-peaked effect on predicted bike demand. Contributions are deeply negative in the early morning hours (roughly midnight to 5 a.m.), meaning the model strongly suppresses predicted rentals during those hours, reaching its lowest point around 4 a.m. Demand rises sharply through the morning commute hours, peaking around 8 a.m., dips slightly in the midday period, then climbs again to its highest point around 5 p.m. (hour 17), before declining steadily through the late evening.

[IMPORTANCE] With an importance score of 0.83, `hr` is by far the single most influential feature in the model — more than four times as important as the next-ranked features (`yr` and `temp`, each around 0.20). In other words, the hour of the day is the dominant driver of predicted demand, overshadowing all other factors combined.

[RECOMMENDATION] Because demand is concentrated in two sharp daily peaks — the morning commute (~8 a.m.) and the evening commute (~5 p.m.) — bike availability and staffing for rebalancing should be prioritised around those specific hours, while resources can be scaled back substantially during the early morning hours (midnight to 5 a.m.) when demand is at its lowest.
